scenario.summary: Attackers gain initial access by exploiting vulnerabilities in public-facing applications or by tricking users into executing malicious files on endpoints. Once inside, they leverage over-privileged cloud identities to perform resource discovery while masquerading as legitimate administrative users. The intrusion is further concealed using multi-hop proxies and Tor to obfuscate the origin of their cloud API activity.

hunt.name: Initial Access and Execution via Exposed Writable Paths
hunt.description: This hunt unmasks the transition from external vulnerability to local execution by correlating internet-facing asset exposure with suspicious behavioral patterns in user-writable paths. Following the behavioral clustering research from Unit 42, we prioritize hosts that demonstrate both high-severity vulnerabilities and rare file executions. The hunt identifies binaries running from paths like Downloads, /tmp, or AppData, baselines them against the fleet, and corroborates the activity with script and network telemetry.

config.content: SELECT domain_or_ip, ip_address, port, product, version FROM hb_exposed_assets WHERE product IS NOT NULL
config.description: Identify the external attack surface to focus behavioral analysis on hosts that are directly reachable from the internet.
config.expected_signal: A list of IP addresses and domains representing the external footprint. Silence means no assets are externally exposed according to the scanner.

primitive_config.label: Identify Internet-Exposed Assets
primitive_config.content: SELECT domain_or_ip, ip_address, port, product, version FROM hb_exposed_assets WHERE product IS NOT NULL
primitive_config.expected: A list of IP addresses and domains representing the external footprint. Silence means no assets are externally exposed according to the scanner.

config.content: SELECT device_uid, cve_uid, affected_package_name, severity_id FROM hb_vulnerability_finding WHERE severity_id >= 4
config.description: Narrow the hunt to hosts with high-severity vulnerabilities (T1190) which serve as candidates for exploitation.
config.expected_signal: A list of host identifiers with critical/high vulnerabilities. Silence proves no high-severity vulnerabilities were found by scanners.

primitive_config.label: High-Severity Vulnerability Scope
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_uid, cve_uid, affected_package_name, severity_id FROM hb_vulnerability_finding WHERE severity_id >= 4
primitive_config.expected: A list of host identifiers with critical/high vulnerabilities. Silence proves no high-severity vulnerabilities were found by scanners.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_path, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\temp\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/tmp/%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/home/%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/var/tmp/%') AND (instr(',' || '{{suspicious_extensions}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(SUBSTR(process_name, -4)) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{suspicious_extensions}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(SUBSTR(process_name, -3)) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Find binaries executing from non-system, user-writable directories (T1204.002).
config.expected_signal: Binary execution in paths like Downloads, AppData/Local/Temp, or /tmp. Silence does not prove absence, as attackers may masquerade as system services.

primitive_config.label: Suspicious Executions in Writable Paths
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_name, process_path, process_cmd_line, user_name, time FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\temp\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/tmp/%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/home/%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/var/tmp/%') AND (instr(',' || '{{suspicious_extensions}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(SUBSTR(process_name, -4)) || ',') > 0 OR instr(',' || '{{suspicious_extensions}}' || ',', ',' || LOWER(SUBSTR(process_name, -3)) || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
primitive_config.expected: Binary execution in paths like Downloads, AppData/Local/Temp, or /tmp. Silence does not prove absence, as attackers may masquerade as system services.

config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) AS path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\temp\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/tmp/%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/home/%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY LOWER(process_path) HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
config.description: Stack-count the identified paths to isolate rare, unique payloads from common user behavior (like Slack or Teams updates).
config.expected_signal: A list of rare file paths. Paths seen fleet-wide are likely benign software updates.

primitive_config.label: Prevalence of Writable Path Binaries
primitive_config.content: SELECT LOWER(process_path) AS path, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_process_activity WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\temp\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/tmp/%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/home/%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY LOWER(process_path) HAVING hosts <= 3 ORDER BY hosts ASC
primitive_config.expected: A list of rare file paths. Paths seen fleet-wide are likely benign software updates.

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_path, dst_endpoint_ip, direction, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/tmp/%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/home/%') AND direction = 'outbound' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Identify potential C2 connections originating from the suspicious processes identified in previous steps.
config.expected_signal: Network connections from the same paths as the suspicious binaries. Normal apps (browsers) should be filtered by the agent.

primitive_config.label: Outbound Activity from Writable Paths
primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, process_path, dst_endpoint_ip, direction, time FROM hb_network_connection WHERE (LOWER(process_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/tmp/%' OR LOWER(process_path) LIKE '/home/%') AND direction = 'outbound' AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')

config.content: SELECT device_hostname, script_content, actor_user_name, time FROM hb_script_activity WHERE (LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%-enc%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%iex%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%curl%|%sh%' OR LOWER(script_content) LIKE '%wget%|%sh%') AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days')
config.description: Detect obfuscated scripts that often drop or support the execution of malicious payloads (T1204.002).
config.expected_signal: Script blocks containing encoded commands or one-liners associated with payload staging.

config.objective: Identify hosts that are (1) internet-exposed or highly vulnerable, AND (2) running rare processes from writable paths, AND (3) showing script or network corroboration. Cite specific process paths and PIDs.
config.description: Correlate exposure, vulnerability status, and behavioral signals to identify confirmed host compromises.
config.expected_signal: A per-host verdict of malicious, suspicious, or benign.
config.success_criteria: A verdict for every candidate host citing row evidence.

config.question: The triage verdict is malicious for at least one host.
config.condition: The triage verdict is malicious for at least one host.
config.description: Route confirmed compromises to isolation and others to review.
Prevent further malicious activity on a confirmed compromised host.
config.instructions: Isolate the host from the network. Capture volatile artifacts if possible before full termination.

config.description: Perform manual confirmation of the breach and identify the root cause exploit.
config.instructions: Review the cited process PIDs and paths. Determine if the initial access was via the identified vulnerability (T1190) or if a user executed a file manually (T1204.002).

config.description: Document the negative result or benign findings for future baselining.
config.instructions: If no threats were found, document the findings as evidence of absence for these stages. Record any benign software paths discovered to tune future runs.
